answer: Treat each new agent as a vertex that earns voting weight only after its bond survives a long horizon, say ninety days, with slashing if peers prove it duplicated another agent's work. A sybil farm can spawn thousands of keys cheaply, but each must lock capital for the full horizon while producing distinct output; an answer that is merely an echo of a sibling's text triggers a slash across every bonded copy, so splitting one operator into many identities multiplies risk, not influence.
